What sin is in this? Hear it well from me yourself, best one. A falsehood should never be spoken, even with life in the throat.
naradapuran:152:56	One should practise truth alone, established in truth, which is dharma directly. Brahma stands in truth, the good stand in truth.
naradapuran:152:57	The whole world, moving and unmoving, always stands in truth. 'Speak the truth' — this saying is sung in the Vedanta.
naradapuran:152:58	Truth is of the nature of Brahman; let us meditate on that truth. Truth, O Brahmin, is always auspicious and the giver of auspiciousness.
naradapuran:152:59	Untruth destroys the self and quickly creates conviction; truth is not to be told to women — hear the reason there too.
naradapuran:152:60	'One should not tell a treasure to a woman' — in the beginning a prevention of fault is said; it generates dharma and shows the subtlety of dharma.
naradapuran:152:61	Kusha, Brahmins, water, fire, the Vedas, earth, time, directions and gods as witnesses: where in marriages these are, that is called marriage.
naradapuran:152:62	The rite of 'accepting together' is prescribed in marriage; in the twice-born initiation it is shown for teacher and disciple of woman and man.
naradapuran:152:63	Therefore bride and groom are to be known as teacher and disciple of each other; not even an atom of difference between them is to be perceived by the knower.
naradapuran:152:64	By conformity to each one's action, in the primacy of woman and of the appointed, if there is a fault of reversal, fate alone is the cause here.
naradapuran:152:65	The whole world with gods, demons and men is subject to fate. Fate is the impressions of actions accumulated in earlier births.
naradapuran:152:66	Each, enjoying what is gained, acts as the doer of desire; whether auspicious or inauspicious, O Brahmin, the wise know that as peace.
naradapuran:152:67	A peaceful creature of true conduct is a saviour of the world. Knowing this, this husband was not killed by me;
naradapuran:152:68	purified by being freed from the sin of destroying virginity, by my service, he has gone, struck down by your hand, to the state of the meritorious.
naradapuran:152:69	I, knowing the subtlety of dharma, did a favour for my husband; in saving your life, O best of Brahmins, dharma was mine.
naradapuran:152:70	Hear well what was obtained by that dharma: I had attained a demoness's womb as the demon's beloved,
naradapuran:152:71	but a Brahmin woman of desired form was born by the force of dharma. Dharma is the wish-granting cow; contentment is the garden Nandana;
naradapuran:152:72	knowledge is declared the giver of liberation; thirst is the river Vaitarani. Falling into the Vaitarani, my husband was lifted by me; he became here (a good man).
naradapuran:152:73	And for this one, O Brahmin, having been placed in a house of the highest class, she will be a wife, unattached, in her father's house.
naradapuran:152:74	I shall always be the guardian of you and her, teacher of dharma. She who was your wife before union with me,
naradapuran:152:75	this one will be your companion wife, fair-faced one; she too, having reached an animal state, is freed by my favour.
naradapuran:152:76	I, long ago in a former life, was a woman, the beauty of the world, known as Kandali, daughter of the sage Aurva, O Brahmin.
naradapuran:152:77	By the power of austerity I became a twin-bearer; my male companion was tamed for the cause of dharma.
naradapuran:152:78	By that same Aurva I, the remaining one, was given to Durvasas. Having got him as husband, O best of Brahmins, I fell under the force of past karma;
naradapuran:152:79	delighting in quarrels, cursed by my husband, I became ashes; with a remnant of sin I came into a she-demon's womb.
naradapuran:152:80	In that womb I got this husband, king of demons, the brilliant Gobhila, who has been struck down by you.
naradapuran:152:81	His curse in youth, O best of Brahmins; for a certain king's daughter, the woman's death was begun by you.
naradapuran:152:82	I, freed from the she-demon state by the strength of my earlier good deed, became your helper.
naradapuran:152:83	I was made unhappy by my husband, because he had carried off the maiden before; then, O Brahmin, that sinner was killed by me.
naradapuran:152:84	Because you trusted me with all your heart, therefore I shall protect you with my whole being, lover.
naradapuran:152:85	This is my true oath, witnessed by the five elements, spoken by me in the presence of the whole Person here.
naradapuran:152:86	O best of Brahmins, do not ever act otherwise in agreement; you must stay by my word in all affairs, honourable one.
Hearing these words spoken by the she-demon, he accepted all that she had done then.
Then the she-demon, taking all the treasure of the cave, having become a female elephant and placing my husband on her back,
with that wide-eyed one, with a jewel necklace, joyful, went by the sky path toward Kashi, O lovely-eyed one.

O sole doer of the work of destroying the family of Danu's sons, sinless, mounted on the serpent-king, Kamsa's death! Eyes of sun and moon, bold in action, dispeller of darkness, dark as a new cloud, Lord!
naradapuran:153:46	O sacrificer, bearer of sacrifice, bound by his mother with a rope, fond of butter, Lord of the cowherd hosts, slayer of Agha, Baka, the bull demon, Keshi, Putana, Trishiras, Vali, and the ten-headed one!
naradapuran:153:47	Destroyer of Naraka and Mura, cutter of Bana's arms, worshipped by the enemy of Tripura (Shiva), friend of Sudama, to be served, whose lotus feet are a boat for crossing samsara, of manifest lordship, ancient, full-armed!
naradapuran:153:48	Attainable by the merit of many births, fit for auspiciousness, known by the Veda, abode of the Veda, peaceful, pure! Your pair of feet is the choicest boon; I have come to you for refuge, afflicted by sin — protect me!
naradapuran:153:49	I have no other giver of goal than the Primal Person; be gracious to my prayer, O pure one.
Thus praised with devotion by the god Shambhu, the Lord of the world, Madhava, loving to devotees, suddenly appeared.
Seeing him, Hara fell on the ground like a staff before Hari; rising again, O best of Brahmins, he bowed with folded hands.
Hrishikesha said to the leader of spirits who had bowed: "Choose a boon; I shall give it, pleased with your hymn."
Hearing the Lord's words, the lord of spirits, tormented by the guilt of Brahmin-slaying, said to Hari, giver of enjoyment and liberation:

I wish to stay in your field, O bearer of discus and mace. If the guilt of Brahmin-slaying is seen standing outside the limit of your field,
naradapuran:153:55	show mercy to me by giving me the field, Garuda-bannered; when I leave, the guilt of Brahmin-slaying will come to me again.
naradapuran:153:56	Staying in your field I shall receive worship in the three worlds. Having said so, the Bull-bannered One became silent before the God of gods.
The beloved of the daughter of the Milk Ocean said "So be it." From then, O best of Brahmins, this is called Shiva's field.
But the wise know this field as Keshava's, ancient, O best of Brahmins, of Madhava who was filled with compassion.
Water flowed from his eyes, and from it Bindusara (Bindu lake) arose; at Madhava's command the Bull-bannered God bathed there.
As soon as Hari (Shiva) bathed, that skull fell from his hand; that holy place became famed by the name Kapalamochana.
Madhava, named Bindumadhava, giving his own abode to the trident-bearer, and Shambhu, bound by devotion, remained there.
Whom Brahma and the other gods in heaven always see, surrounded by the naked ones, bright as ten thousand suns,
obstacles were made to his service by the trident-bearer, dear one; those overcome by those obstacles, worshippers of Shiva, praising Vishnu,
all the people stand here, thinking "Shiva is Kashi." By thinking of Shiva, O Brahmin, all Shaivas are untroubled.
They go to Shiva's world, free from old age and death. The good, endowed with much merit, live here free of disease,
eating the remnants of sacrifice, O husband of Kashi, rich in prosperity. They do not praise bathing, chanting or worship of gods here,
nor giving, O best of Brahmins, except the one thing: the falling of the body. A man desiring death attains death and surely becomes one whose task is done.
This city, filled with palaces, reached, O Brahmin, gives liberation even to a woman of pleasure; what then of the vow-keepers?
Let this girl be placed here in Kashi's lord's temple, separated earlier by that wicked demon,
a maiden keeping vows for her own union. This is the power of this field, beneficial, O best of Brahmins:
here deeds, auspicious and inauspicious, past, future, done knowingly or unknowingly, are destroyed.
This city was long ago made by Krishna for the destruction of actions; those who die in it do not experience the endless dreadful torments of Yama."
She accepted all that was said by her with affection. When the king's word was accepted, the pleased she-demon said:

By your word let my daughter be the Brahmin's servant; abandoning co-wife rivalry, protect my daughter.
naradapuran:154:36	You are, without doubt, mistress of my daughter, of my wife, of my powerful people, of the city and the realm.
naradapuran:154:37	She will always stay by your word. Hearing that, Sudyumna's night-ranging companion
with a pure heart approved, and said to the king who was ready to give:

O best of kings, for the reason that you bowed to me with good feeling, let this be the second wife of this twice-born.
naradapuran:154:40	And I should be worshipped by you, having made worship in the temple of the goddess, with all citizens, in the bright fortnight of Phalguna:
naradapuran:154:41	a festival of seven days from the eighth to the fourteenth with actors, dancers, abundant song and music,
naradapuran:154:42	and with worship by offerings of mead, meat and blood. Thus doing for you I shall always bring welfare,
naradapuran:154:43	O tiger among kings; keep your word. Hearing her words King Sudyumna
said lovingly to the Brahmin: "Take this king's daughter also as wife, O best of Brahmins, auspicious, by the rule stated in the domestic texts.
Giving up jealousy, I shall be a sister to this wide-eyed one." By the she-demon's word, having married the king's daughter,
the Brahmin, with much wealth, went to Mahodayapura, climbing on the she-demon in her elephant form, in a moment.
Then I heard, goddess, that your husband had arrived, joined with wealth and jewels, with two wives.
Then I was reproached many times by relatives, parents and friends with harsh words that pierced the vitals:

How will you go to your husband, greedy for wealth, surrounded by prosperity, whom you earlier abandoned as poor, as a wretch?
naradapuran:154:51	Wealth is fickle; the fathers' property of women, it is said, is steady when earned by the husband.

How could he speak to one whom he rebuked with harsh words? Even entering his house will be difficult for him.
naradapuran:154:53	Even if you go there, sleeping with the husband will never be pleasant, O ill-conducted one.
naradapuran:154:54	If your husband takes you for fear of public blame, with a heart devoid of love he will never meet you.
naradapuran:154:55	Nothing in the world is so painful as the meeting of a couple with distant minds; it causes great disarray.
Hearing many such words from relatives, with face down and eyes full of tears, I became very unhappy.
Worshipped in mind, but deluded by earlier greed, I had not given my hand's bracelet or girdle,
nor even given anklets, by which a husband would be satisfied. The husband is called the lord of wealth and life in the world.

The wealth was taken by me; what will be my fate? How shall I go to his house, how speak with him again?
naradapuran:154:60	How will he receive me, whom I, wicked, abandoned? As I thought so, my heart in pain,
surrounded by relatives, a palanquin arrived, shining, very soft, with an umbrella bright as the moon,
spread with soft wool, borne on the shoulders of strong men. Those men came and said to me again and again, O auspicious one:

You are called by your husband; go quickly, joyful. Your husband has come with wealth and jewels, with a good wife.
naradapuran:154:64	As soon as he entered the house, we were quickly sent by your husband to fetch you, who are in your father's house.
Then I, ashamed, goddess, seeing my husband's action, gave no reply to them and remained somewhat silent.
Then I was exhorted by relatives again and again: "Called by your lord, go to him with honour.
A wife who, called by her husband, does not go to him becomes a crow for fifteen births, daughter."
Having said so and reassured me, they took me hurriedly, put me on the palanquin, and affectionately said again and again, "Go."
Then those men, placing the palanquin on their shoulders, quickly went to Mahodayapura, where my husband lived.
I saw his house all covered with gold, furnished with seats, food, wealth and clothes.
Then the she-demon goddess and also the king's daughter, with love and devotion, bowed to me, O fair one.
Then I was honoured by them both with love as was proper; pleased by my husband's word, bathed, I was brought food.
After sunset my husband quickly called me, embraced me long with his arms, and seated me on a couch.
Then calling the night-ranger and the king's daughter, he said: "With devotion you two must serve her feet.
She is my first wife and elder to you both." At the husband's word, my feet were then held by them,
both giving up the jealousy born of co-wife rivalry, O fair-eyed one. Then my husband, calling servants, said:

Whatever wealth I obtained earlier from the demon, and everything I got from the king when I married his daughter,
naradapuran:154:78	bring it all with devotion, without delay. This is the mistress; you are servants of that wealth.
By his word the servants brought the wealth at once, auspicious one; the husband, joyful, offered all of it.
Honouring me with ornaments, clothes and ... with a sincere heart, in the sight of both the she-demon and the king's daughter,
he embraced me seated on the couch and kissed my lower lip. Seeing that wonder — the husband's offering of body and wealth —
hearing a delighting word and having my breasts pressed by his hand, I seemed to have my life struck like Gauri cut by a sword.
Then I reached the hell-torment ordered by Yama; passing through it, in great pain, I became a wooden (house-lizard), auspicious one.
I shall again go to animal wombs a thousand times: the woman who does not preserve her husband's wealth and life, fair-faced one,
she too will surely reach such a state, without doubt. Knowing this, one should always guard the husband's wealth and life.
Husband, mother, father, wealth, life, teacher and goal.
A woman goes with her husband, through great merit, from the burning of her own body to Vishnu's abode; one greedy for wealth and body goes to Yama's torments and a wretched womb.
gave a sight of himself to those tormented by demons. Seeing the God of gods, Vaikuntha, tender of heart,
they respectfully prayed for the quick killing of Virochana. Hearing the matter of Shakra and the others, the best of those who know what is to be done
reassured the gods with love and sent them off joyfully. When the hosts of gods had gone, the best knower of all means,
in the form of an old Brahmin, went to Virochana's house, arrived at the time of honouring Brahmins, the accomplisher of the task.
Seeing that Brahmin, the wide-eyed lady, joyful of heart, with unprecedented devotion honoured him and gave him a seat.
He, refusing the seat given, said to her, auspicious one: "I do not accept the supreme seat given by you, goddess.
Hear my incomparable task for which I have come; having understood my intent, honourable one,
whoever accepts that, I shall take worship from him, fair-faced one." Hearing the old Brahmin's words, the lady skilled in speech,
deluded by Vishnu's maya and greatly delighted by womanhood, said: "Whatever is in your mind, O Brahmin, I shall give; accept it.
Give me a seat and foot-water, that gives the desired." Thus told, the Brahmin said: "I do not trust a woman's word;
if your husband says it, then I shall have trust." Hearing what the Brahmin said, the mistress of Virochana's house
summoned her husband right there in the Brahmin's presence. By the messenger's word, the son of Prahlada (Virochana) came delighted
to the inner apartments where his wife, the wide-eyed lady, was. Seeing her husband arrived, the devoted wife,
rising and bowing, offered the best Brahmin the seat again. When he did not accept the seat given with respect,
she told the king, her husband, the lord of the demons. Hearing that matter, the king of demons Virochana,
deluded by love for his wife, agreed to all that. Once the demon agreed, understanding his mind,
the Brahmin said joyfully: "Grant me your own life." Then the couple, bewildered by their own remorse,
after meditating a moment, with joined hands, said to the Brahmin: "Take our life, Brahmin, give us your foot-water.
The word spoken by you we make true; obtain our love." Then the Brahmin, with joy, accepting the seat,
Janardana, pleased, gave her foot-water with devotion. Having washed the Brahmin's feet, the wide-eyed lady, glad,
with her husband put on her head the water of the washed feet. Then at once, fair-browed one, the couple in divine form
boarded the best aerial car and went to Vishnu's abode. Then the Lord Vishnu, pleased, having removed the gods' thorn,
went to the abode of Vaikuntha, praised by all the hosts of gods. Thus I too must give what I promised you, goddess."
